title: Session debug probe checklist + sketch notes
body:
Purpose:
Provide an operationally useful, light-weight console surface that lets engineers and on-call responders move from a symptom (timeout / 5xx / model error) to a reproducible investigation and handoff within a single session view. This doc collects UX notes, quick wireframe descriptions, a probe checklist for incident handoff, and an initial groomed backlog.

Audience:
- SRE/On-call engineers who need to triage failing requests quickly
- Product/Platform engineers reproducing/patching model-serving issues
- Customer-facing CS/Support when preparing a reproducible bug report for eng

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Fast context: show the minimal set of request/session metadata up front (route, model variant, model hash, region, client id, auth tier, token counts, latency percentile).
2) Repro steps in three clicks: copy prompt+headers, re-run with controlled env, attach toggles for KV cache and quantization variant.
3) Error-first timeline: show only events that impacted the failure path (timeouts, queue drops, 5xx, model runtime exceptions), collapsed by default but expandable to full traces.
4) Lightweight traces: avoid full distributed trace by default — show high-signal spans (proxy, gateway, runtime, model, fallback).
5) Handoff checklist: structured minimal reproduction + known mitigations + links to cost/throughput telemetry.

Primary screen (session probe summary) - wireframe notes:
- Header bar: session id, short-status chip (TIMEOUT / 5xx / MODEL_ERR / OK), primary action buttons [Re-run], [Export as ZIP], [Create Incident].
- Left column (50%): request snapshot card: prompt snippet (first 512 tokens), input size, content-type, user-supplied metadata labels, model variant, model checksum (click-to-copy). Copy actions: copy-prompt, copy-header, copy-full-request.
- Right column (50%): failure insights card: top two probable causes (heuristic), quick metrics (p95 latency at time T, GPU mem spike?), fallback count, cache hit/miss ratio. Small inline timeline micro-chart (sparkline) with markers for key events.
- Expandable timeline: below columns, chronological list with lightweight spans: gateway -> auth -> routing -> queue -> runtime -> model -> backend-call. Each span shows duration, error code, sample logs (1-2 lines), link to full trace in APM.

Probe checklist (to show as 'Handoff checklist' panel on the right in narrow view):
- Checklist items (checkbox + timestamp):
  - Reproduce locally? [ ] - steps recorded
  - Re-run with same model and seed? [ ]
  - Toggle cache off and re-run? [ ]
  - Attach full request zip? [ ]
  - Attach first-failure trace id? [ ]
  - Note traffic conditions (burst, warm-up)? [ ]
  - Suggested owner (SRE / runtime / model oncall) [ ]
- Each item expands into micro-instructions. Example: 'Toggle cache off and re-run' -> button that launches a sandbox replay using the exact request and a toggle for KV-cache=false. Output of that run gets appended as a new session child.

Error cards (compact variants used in lists):
- Visuals: small icon for class (clock for timeout, bomb for 5xx, puzzle for model-exception), short title (e.g., "runtime: out-of-memory during token 842"), severity badge, counts (occurrences in last 1h/24h). Click opens session view.

Interaction patterns and microcopy suggestions:
- For timeouts: show 'time waited' vs 'server responded at' and a speculative hint: "Likely queue pressure — consider increasing burst capacity or reducing batch size for route X." (hint only visible to internal roles).
- For 5xx: surface last upstream status and first upstream exception. Microcopy: "5xx at runtime—could be model kernel crash or OOM. Attach raw runtime logs and kernel version."
- For model errors (bad output): show 'quality regression' toggle that pins evaluation prompt, compares to baseline model (side-by-side diffs) and shows recent rollout changes.

Telemetry panels to include (collapsible):
- Token-level cost breakdown for the session (encoder/decoder split)
- GPU memory / utilization around the window (+/- 10s)
- Queue length and scheduler delays
- Autoscaler activity (if Dedicated)

Accessibility & roles:
- By default, latest logs are redacted for external-facing roles (customer success), with a 'Show internal logs' toggle for internal staff.
- Export ZIP removes PII by default; include an 'Include full request' checkbox that requires two-step confirmation.

Backlog grooming (prioritized short list):
1) Attachable sandbox re-run: button launches ephemeral replay with toggles (cache on/off, quantization level, model-variant). Acceptance: replay finishes < 30s for small requests and is linked as child session. (JIRA-RED-4128)
2) Compact error-card list with severity sorting and group-by-route. Acceptance: list renders 5k rows and pagination works. (JIRA-RED-4201)
3) Inline timeline span collapsing and trace-linking UX. Acceptance: user can jump from span -> full APM trace in <2 clicks. (JIRA-RED-4250)
4) 'Quality regression' comparator: golden prompt diffs between two model versions. Acceptance: side-by-side diff rendering and pass/fail heuristics. (JIRA-RED-4302)
5) Handoff template generator: builds incident body pre-filled for PagerDuty/Confluence. Acceptance: 80% of incidents can use generated template without edits. (JIRA-RED-4333)

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: what fields must always be cropped for exported zips? Legal needs a small review. Action: schedule review with legal (Nina).
- Performance: replay sandbox might add cost — need to cap per-org monthly replays. Ops: add quota gating.
- Noise: heuristics for 'probable cause' will require telemetry tuning to avoid false positives. Small experiment suggested: A/B show vs not-show.

Notes from whiteboard session (sketch fragments transcribed):
- Sketch A: session header with inline quick-filters (Error type, severity, route).
- Sketch B: two-pane with timeline collapsed to dots; click dot -> open trace sandwich.
- Sketch C: handoff modal that pre-fills owner and suggested remediation steps (rollback, increase capacity, change batch size).

Short sample acceptance criteria for 'Re-run' feature:
- UI exposes a 'Re-run' modal with at most 4 toggles: cache on/off, model-variant select, seed, simulate-low-memory.
- Running a replay creates a new session linked to the original, shows logs, and tags owner as 'replay-bot'.
- Replay outputs are rate-limited to avoid abuse and billed to customer's usage.

Next steps (immediate):
- Align with SRE on required telemetry fields (Liam). Blocker if missing.
- Prototype low-fidelity mockups in Figma for primary screen and handoff modal (Nina).
- Create engineering spike to validate sandbox replay prototype (Ethan, 2w).

References and related docs:
- TODO: link to existing 'triage quickstart' doc and 'investigator triage workbench' (these are earlier drafts).
- Confluence: Session Debug Playbook (linked above).

Unresolved UX decisions to schedule for design sync:
- Should 'Quality regression' be opt-in per org? (privacy + cost)
- Inline APM embedding vs link-out (APM licensing concerns)

Quick sketch ASCII (for context) - very rough:
[ Header: session-12345 ] [ TIMEOUT ] [Re-run] [Export]
-------------------------------
| Request card      | Insights  |
| prompt: "Once upon a..."| probable cause: queue pressure |
| tokens: 1,228     | p95 latency: 2.3s at 14:03 |
-------------------------------
[ timeline ] -> gateway(10ms) -> router(5ms) -> queue(1200ms, dropped) -> runtime(---)

If you want, I can convert these notes into a 4-frame Figma brief and a single-page spec that the eng team can estimate from.

Author notes: this is intentionally light-weight and purposely leaves implementation details (APM vendor, exact trace ids) negotiable until SRE sync.

Maya Singh
Product Manager, Console
